messages:
Maria: Heads up — customer onboarding hit a wall with our Python async client and their corporate forward proxy. Async requests fail during TLS handshake with 'unknown ca'. Sync path worked after setting REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, but async still dies.

Maria: Repro (trimmed):
```python
# redwood-python 1.0.0b2 (httpx)
import os
from redwood import AsyncRedwoodClient
os.environ['REDWOOD_BASE_URL'] = 'https://private.customer.internal'
os.environ['REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE'] = '/opt/certs/corp-root.pem'
client = AsyncRedwoodClient(api_key='s.xxxx', base_url=os.environ['REDWOOD_BASE_URL'])
await client.embeddings.create(model='embed-1', input=['a'])
# -> ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] unable to get local issuer certificate
```

Kevin: Did you try trust_env=True? httpx by default won't read REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE unless trust_env is enabled (and env proxies are set). Also certifi can mask SSL_CERT_FILE on some installs.

Maria: We couldn't pass trust_env to AsyncRedwoodClient; the constructor doesn't accept any httpx kwargs. The typed pyi only lists (api_key, base_url, timeout, headers). We had to monkeypatch _create_httpx_client to inject trust_env=True and a custom ssl_context.

Ling: That sounds like an API gap. Two gaps: (1) need explicit ssl_context or verify param to allow custom ca bundles; (2) need clear behavior doc for env var precedence. Also our type stubs should include **kwargs passthrough with typed names, maybe a TypedDict?

SDK-bot: Note: Issue created — SDK-4570 'Expose httpx transport/ssl options in AsyncRedwoodClient' (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python/issues/4570). Labels: devex, sdk, p2.

Kevin: For immediate workaround, you can construct an httpx.AsyncClient with a custom transport and monkeypatch the client's _httpx_client attribute. Example:
```python
import ssl, httpx
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile='/opt/certs/corp-root.pem')
transport = httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(ssl_context=ctx, trust_env=True)
client._httpx_client = httpx.AsyncClient(transport=transport)
```
But that's internal and untyped.

Jordan: Suggestion: add explicit params to AsyncRedwoodClient signature: verify: Union[bool, str, ssl.SSLContext]=True, trust_env: bool=False, proxies: Optional[Dict[str,str]]=None. Keep them optional and documented. Also update py.typed and pyi to expose types for mypy.

Ling: Also consider adding an env var REDWOOD_TRUST_BUNDLE that our code checks before falling back to certifi/SSL_CERT_FILE to make behavior deterministic. Docs should show precedence: REDWOOD_TRUST_BUNDLE > SSL_CERT_FILE > REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE > certifi.where().

Maria: One weirdness: customer environment had HTTP_PROXY set but no HTTPS_PROXY. httpx picks up proxies only for http(s) when trust_env True and HTTPS_PROXY present. That explains why sync requests (requests lib) worked but async didn't in some images. We should add a note in onboarding checklist to verify both HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY.

Kevin: For SNI issues: if their proxy terminates TLS and reissues certs, server_hostname must match the cert presented. If base_url host and SNI host differ, we need a way to override server_hostname in the SSLContext. Proposal: allow base_url and an optional sni_host param. Example: AsyncRedwoodClient(..., sni_host='models.customer.internal'). We'll document it's for private deployments only.

Ling: Please include small tests in SDK repo that spin up an httpx test server with custom CA and proxy to catch regressions. Also add a typing test (pyright/mypy) to ensure pyi matches implementation.

Maria: I'll paste the minimal monkeypatch + repro into SDK-4570. For the onboarding docs: add a 'Private/Dedicated networking checklist' with examples for Linux/Mac/Windows and electron.

SDK-bot: Linked PR draft: #4582 - expose verify, trust_env, sni_host on AsyncRedwoodClient (draft). Assigned to Kevin.

Kevin: I'll flesh out the PR — will add both sync and async overloads, keep defaults secure (verify=True), and add a short DX note about not recommending verify=False. We should also log a warning if REDWOOD_TRUST_BUNDLE path doesn't exist.

Maria: Thanks all. Leaving updates on SDK-4570/PR-4582. If anyone from infra can double-check edge SNI behavior for private endpoints, that'd help avoid adding awkward hacks.

Jordan: I'll ping infra and post the edge behavior note in that issue.
